explained.tdh.wallets.meta.title: Your wallets · 6529 Explained
explained.tdh.wallets.meta.description: Why your TDH changed, and how up to four wallets count as one collector.
explained.tdh.wallets.title: Up to four wallets count as one collector.
explained.tdh.wallets.lede: Link your wallets both ways, and their copies, days and one boost count together; a fourth needs fresh links, made on or after {date}.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.label: First question
explained.tdh.wallets.why.title: Why did my number change? Pick what happened.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.moved: I moved a copy between my own wallets
explained.tdh.wallets.why.sold: I sold or sent a copy away
explained.tdh.wallets.why.newcard: Nothing, but a new card came out
explained.tdh.wallets.why.movedVerdict: It keeps its age only inside one identity.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.movedBody: If both wallets were in one identity, linked both ways, the copy kept its days; your total moves only by rounding, about one TDH for each card moved, more with a boost. If not, the copy started again at zero, and if that copy was what completed your season or full set, the boost of the identity it left drops too. Link the two wallets both ways and it gets its days back. A common cause is one pair not linked both ways:
explained.tdh.wallets.why.movedCaption: A–B and B–C, but no A–C: B and C count together, A alone. A wallet joins only if it is linked with every member.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.movedAria: A linked with B, B linked with C, but A and C not linked: {groups}.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.addedVerdict: Your wallets were split for a while.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.addedBody: Until the new wallet's last link confirms, your wallets can count as two identities, each with its own boost. A snapshot in that window counts them apart. Sign with the new wallet last, in one batch: {how}.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.soldBody: A copy's days leave with the copy. When you sell one of several copies of a card, the one you received last goes first, so your oldest copies keep counting. If the copy completed a season or a full set, your boost drops with it.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.unlinkedBody: The grouping on the snapshot day applies to all history. Copies moved between those wallets before now count from when they arrived in their current wallet. Linking again gives the age back.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.newcardVerdict: A full set waits for the new card.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.newcardBody: A full set means every card that counts, and each new card counts a day after its first mint. One full set loses nothing, because complete seasons still count. If you hold more than one full set, the extra-set part of your boost pauses until you hold that many copies of the new card.
explained.tdh.wallets.why.explain: Explain my TDH shows what your identity held and counted in the latest result.
explained.tdh.wallets.rule.label: The rule
explained.tdh.wallets.rule.title: Every pair links both ways, and the most recently confirmed link decides.
explained.tdh.wallets.rule.body: Wallets become one identity when every pair among them is linked in both directions. The group is built from the most recently confirmed link outward. Up to three wallets group as before. A fourth joins only when one wallet has links both ways with each of the other three, all registered from {gate}.
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.label: Four wallets, one identity
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.question: How do wallets become one identity, and when can a fourth join?
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.step1: risky: D's links one by one, {step}
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.batch: safe: D signs last, in one batch
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.caption: Grey lines: linked both ways before {date}. Blue lines: linked both ways from {date}. A dashed wallet counts alone.
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.sayFive: {alone} counts on its own. The group is built from the newest confirmed link, so linking a fifth wallet can push an older one out (D136).
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.sayMissing: Every pair must be linked both ways. A wallet joins a group only if it is linked with every member.
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.saySplit: until D's last link confirms. A snapshot taken now counts two identities, each with its own boost.
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.sayBatch: D's three links go in one batch transaction, so they confirm in one block and no snapshot ever sees a smaller group.
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.sayOldFour: Only three count together. A group grows past three only when one wallet has links both ways with each of the others, made on or after {date} (D136).
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.sayOne: One identity: one TDH, one boost, one vote.
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.ruleBoth: a pair counts once linked both ways
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.ruleNewest: newest confirmed link first; links in one block by pair key (the two addresses, sorted)
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.ruleEvery: a wallet joins only if linked with every member
explained.tdh.wallets.lens.ruleGate: past {ungated} only if one member links both ways with each other member, every link registered at or after {gate}
explained.tdh.wallets.add.label: Add a fourth wallet
explained.tdh.wallets.add.title: The new wallet signs last, in one batch.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.oneLead: Your three wallets each link to the new wallet, D.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.one: Nothing changes yet: a link counts only once it is confirmed both ways.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.twoLead: D signs last, with one batch to all three.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.two: Its three links confirm in the same block, and the group becomes four in one step. No snapshot ever sees a split.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.batchCap: one batch: four wallets, one step
explained.tdh.wallets.add.cost: Four transactions, each with a normal network fee: one from each current wallet, then D's batch. A vault whose links are sent by a delegation manager takes one transaction per link.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.resign: Your three wallets' links to each other stay as they are. Only the links with D must be made on or after {date}.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.avoid: Signing D first, or renewing old links, can split your wallets for a while.
explained.tdh.wallets.add.setupNote: The guided setup walks you through this order.
explained.tdh.wallets.before.label: Before you start
explained.tdh.wallets.before.profile: Linking merges your wallets' 6529.io profiles, and that cannot be undone: the profile with the highest rating keeps its handle. A wallet already in another consolidation leaves it.
explained.tdh.wallets.before.key: Each linked wallet can sign in as your profile. If one is compromised, revoke its links from your other wallets straight away.
explained.tdh.wallets.before.votes: If a split lowers your TDH for a day, votes above it in TDH waves are cut, and they are not restored. Cast them again once the group is complete.
explained.tdh.wallets.before.manager: A delegation manager acting for all your wallets can change your consolidation on its own.
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.label: Questions
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.roundQ: Can a move between my linked wallets change my TDH at all?
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.roundA: Only by rounding. Each wallet's base TDH is rounded card by card before your wallets are added together, so each card moved can shift your total by about one TDH, more with a boost.
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.laterQ: If I link two wallets later, do old moves between them get their age back?
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.laterA: Yes. The grouping on the snapshot day applies to all history, so a later link restores the age of copies moved between them earlier. Unlinking takes it away.
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.oldQ: I set up four wallets before {date}. What now?
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.oldA: Old links never form a group of four. Three of them count together, built from the newest link; the fourth is the one left out. Link that one afresh: each of your other three links to it, then it signs last in one batch. The links among the three stay as they are.
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.expireA: No. A link lasts until one of its wallets revokes it.
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.validatorsQ: Is this the rule validators will use?
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.validatorsA: Yes, decided: D136 makes 6529.io's four-wallet rule part of TDH v1.4 (D137), and P26, proposed as the consensus rule, states it exactly. The validator software is built and being tested; so far only 6529's own validators sign, in testing. Meanwhile the daily comparison keeps checking 6529.io against the rule.
explained.tdh.wallets.faq.under: Under the hood: why every pair must link both ways
explained.tdh.wallets.hwk.ruleBody: D136; P26 §6.2 and §6.3 as TDH v1.4 ({head}), checked against 6529.io's own code on {graphs} random link graphs.
explained.tdh.wallets.hwk.modelBody: The TDH v1.4 engine's grouping, run in your browser; it passes all {pass} of P26's grouping vectors.
